states.name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

neighbours.name: Bangladesh
neighbours.note: India's longest land border; open riverine stretches make fencing hard.

neighbours.name: China
neighbours.note: Undemarcated Line of Actual Control in the western, middle and eastern sectors.

neighbours.name: Pakistan
neighbours.note: International Border, Line of Control and the Actual Ground Position Line in Siachen.

neighbours.name: Nepal
neighbours.note: Open border under the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship.

neighbours.name: Myanmar
neighbours.note: Hilly, forested border with the North-East; Free Movement Regime debates.

neighbours.name: Bhutan
neighbours.note: Open border; close hydropower and security ties.

neighbours.name: Afghanistan
neighbours.note: Shares a border with India through Gilgit-Baltistan (in Ladakh, under Pakistan's illegal occupation).

neighbours.name: Sri Lanka
neighbours.note: Maritime neighbour across the Palk Strait.

neighbours.name: Maldives
neighbours.note: Maritime neighbour astride Indian Ocean sea lanes.

chokepoints.name: Strait of Hormuz
chokepoints.connects: Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman
chokepoints.why: Most Gulf oil and LNG bound for India passes here; any disruption hits India's energy security.

chokepoints.name: Bab-el-Mandeb
chokepoints.connects: Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
chokepoints.why: Gateway between the Suez route and the Indian Ocean; piracy and attacks on shipping here raise freight costs for India.

chokepoints.name: Suez Canal
chokepoints.why: Shortest sea route between India and Europe; the 1956 crisis here ended Britain's great-power image.

chokepoints.name: Strait of Malacca
chokepoints.connects: Andaman Sea and South China Sea
chokepoints.why: Busiest route to East Asia; China's dependence on it (the 'Malacca dilemma') shapes its Indian Ocean strategy.

chokepoints.name: Sunda Strait
chokepoints.why: Alternative to Malacca for ships moving between the Indian Ocean and East Asia.

chokepoints.name: Lombok Strait
chokepoints.why: Deep-water alternative to Malacca, used by the largest tankers.

chokepoints.name: Taiwan Strait
chokepoints.connects: East China Sea and South China Sea
chokepoints.why: Flashpoint in China–Taiwan tensions; a large share of global trade and chip supply chains pass nearby.

chokepoints.name: Six Degree Channel
chokepoints.why: India's closest point to the Malacca approaches; makes the Andaman and Nicobar Islands strategically vital.

chokepoints.name: Ten Degree Channel
chokepoints.why: Separates the two island groups on the main shipping lanes into the Bay of Bengal.

chokepoints.name: Nine Degree Channel
chokepoints.connects: Minicoy and the main Lakshadweep islands
chokepoints.why: Major route for ships between West Asia and East Asia, passing close to Lakshadweep.

chokepoints.name: Eight Degree Channel
chokepoints.why: Shipping lane close to India's maritime boundary with the Maldives.

chokepoints.name: Palk Strait
chokepoints.connects: Bay of Bengal and Palk Bay
chokepoints.why: Separates India and Sri Lanka; fishing disputes and the Katchatheevu issue.

chokepoints.name: Mozambique Channel
chokepoints.why: Sea lane along East Africa, where India builds ties with island and coastal states.

chokepoints.name: Strait of Gibraltar
chokepoints.why: Western exit of the Suez–Mediterranean route to Europe and the Americas.

chokepoints.name: Bosphorus
chokepoints.connects: Black Sea and Sea of Marmara
chokepoints.why: Only sea outlet for Black Sea grain and energy exports; disrupted by the Russia–Ukraine war.

chokepoints.name: Panama Canal
chokepoints.why: Links the Atlantic and the Pacific; droughts here show how climate change disrupts trade routes.

features.name: Himalayas
features.why: Young fold mountains from the India–Eurasia collision; block cold Central Asian winds and force monsoon rain on the plains.

features.name: Andes
features.why: Fold mountains on the western edge of South America, where the Nazca Plate dives under the continent; part of the Ring of Fire.

features.name: Rocky Mountains
features.why: Western cordillera of North America, running north–south; they create a rain shadow over the Great Plains.

features.name: Alps
features.why: Fold mountains from the Africa–Eurasia collision; run east–west, so they shelter southern Europe from northern cold.

features.name: Atlas Mountains
features.why: Fold mountains of north-west Africa, also from the Africa–Eurasia collision.

features.name: Zagros Mountains
features.why: Fold belt where the Arabian Plate pushes into Eurasia; rich oil fields lie along its foothills.

features.name: Ural Mountains
features.why: Old, worn-down fold mountains in the interior of a continent; a rare exception to young ranges on continental edges.

features.name: Appalachians
features.why: Very old, eroded fold mountains on the eastern side of North America.

features.name: Great Dividing Range
features.why: Runs along eastern Australia; traps moisture from the Pacific trade winds, leaving the interior dry.

features.name: Hindu Kush
features.why: Range of Afghanistan and northern Pakistan; its passes were historic invasion and trade routes into India.

features.name: Caucasus
features.why: Range between the Black and Caspian seas; a corridor for pipelines and contested borders.

features.name: Tian Shan
features.why: Range of Central Asia; its glaciers feed rivers in a dry region.

features.name: Sahara
features.why: World's largest hot desert, on the western side of a continent around 20–30°N under subtropical high pressure.

features.name: Arabian Desert (Rub' al Khali)
features.why: Hot desert under the subtropical high; sits on huge oil and gas reserves.

features.name: Thar Desert
features.why: India's hot desert in the north-west; high solar potential and desertification risk.

features.name: Sonoran Desert
features.why: Hot desert on the western side of North America, around 30°N, dried further by the cold California current.

features.name: Chihuahuan Desert
features.why: Hot desert of northern Mexico, in the rain shadow of the Sierra Madre ranges.

features.name: Atacama Desert
features.why: One of the driest places on Earth: subtropical high pressure, the cold Peru (Humboldt) current and the Andes rain shadow.

features.name: Namib Desert
features.why: Coastal desert of south-west Africa, kept dry by the cold Benguela current.

features.name: Kalahari
features.why: Semi-arid basin of southern Africa, inland from the Namib.

features.name: Great Victoria Desert
features.why: Largest of Australia's deserts, in the dry western and central interior.

features.name: Great Sandy Desert
features.why: Hot desert of north-western Australia, around 20°S.

features.name: Gobi
features.why: Cold desert of Mongolia and China, dry because it is far inland and in the Himalayan–Tibetan rain shadow.

features.name: Taklimakan
features.why: Cold sandy desert in the Tarim Basin, ringed by high mountains.

features.name: Tibetan Plateau
features.why: Highest plateau on Earth; its summer heating helps drive the Indian monsoon and it feeds Asia's great rivers.

features.name: Deccan Plateau
features.why: Old, stable block of peninsular India; the Deccan traps give black cotton soil and mineral wealth.

features.name: Brazilian Highlands
features.why: Ancient plateau of eastern Brazil, rich in iron ore.

features.name: Great Plains
features.why: Temperate grassland of North America; a wheat and maize belt in the rain shadow of the Rockies.

features.name: North European Plain
features.why: Low, open plain across Europe; an easy route for armies in both World Wars.

features.name: Pampas
features.why: Fertile temperate grasslands of Argentina; wheat and cattle.

features.name: Sahel
features.why: Semi-arid belt south of the Sahara; a classic case of desertification.

features.name: Amazon Basin
features.why: Largest tropical rainforest; a global carbon sink under deforestation pressure.

features.name: Congo Basin
features.why: Second-largest tropical rainforest, astride the Equator.

seas.name: Bay of Bengal
seas.why: Warm, shallow waters and the funnel shape of its head make it a major cyclone basin.

seas.name: Arabian Sea
seas.why: Fewer cyclones than the Bay of Bengal, but warming waters are making them stronger.

seas.name: South China Sea
seas.why: Breeding ground for typhoons, and a contested sea under China's nine-dash line.

seas.name: Gulf of Mexico
seas.why: Warm waters feed Atlantic hurricanes; tornadoes are common inland where its moist air meets dry continental air.

seas.name: Persian Gulf
seas.why: Source of much of India's oil and gas imports; exits through the Strait of Hormuz.

seas.name: Red Sea
seas.why: Links the Suez Canal to the Indian Ocean through Bab-el-Mandeb.

seas.name: Mediterranean Sea
seas.why: Links the Suez route to Europe; site of many world history events.

rivers.name: Nile
rivers.why: Flows north through the Sahara; its waters are shared, and disputed, by Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia.

rivers.name: Amazon
rivers.why: Largest river by volume; drains the Amazon rainforest.

rivers.name: Congo
rivers.why: Crosses the Equator twice, so it carries water all year.

rivers.name: Mississippi
rivers.why: Drains the Great Plains into the Gulf of Mexico; a key inland waterway.

rivers.name: Yangtze
rivers.why: China's longest river; the Three Gorges Dam shows the trade-offs of big dams.

rivers.name: Mekong
rivers.why: Rises in Tibet and flows through six countries; upstream dams in China worry the lower Mekong states.

rivers.name: Danube
rivers.why: Flows through ten countries into the Black Sea; an international waterway.

rivers.name: Ob
rivers.why: Siberian river flowing north into the Arctic Ocean; frozen for much of the year.

pins.name: Boston
pins.event: Boston Tea Party (1773): colonists protest British taxes and the trade monopoly.

pins.name: Philadelphia
pins.event: Declaration of Independence (1776) adopted by the American colonies.

pins.name: Paris
pins.event: Storming of the Bastille (1789) begins the French Revolution.

pins.name: Manchester
pins.event: Centre of the cotton-textile factories of Britain's Industrial Revolution.

pins.name: Tokyo
pins.event: Meiji Restoration (1868): the state drives Japan's rapid 'latecomer' industrialisation.

pins.name: Berlin
pins.event: Berlin Conference (1884–85): European powers set rules for dividing Africa.

pins.name: Sarajevo
pins.event: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand (1914) triggers the First World War.

pins.name: Petrograd (St Petersburg)
pins.event: Russian Revolution (1917); Lenin's New Economic Policy follows in 1921.

pins.name: Versailles
pins.event: Treaty of Versailles (1919) ends the First World War on harsh terms for Germany.

pins.name: New York
pins.event: Wall Street Crash (1929) begins the Great Depression.

pins.name: Hiroshima
pins.event: Atomic bombing (1945) ends the Second World War in Asia.

pins.name: Suez
pins.event: Suez Crisis (1956): Egypt nationalises the canal; the failed Anglo-French invasion ends Britain's great-power image.

pins.name: Accra
pins.event: Ghana (Gold Coast) becomes independent in 1957, the first in sub-Saharan Africa, under Kwame Nkrumah.

pins.name: Kuala Lumpur
pins.event: Malaya becomes independent in 1957 after the Malayan Emergency; ethnic balance shapes the new state.

pins.name: Donbas
pins.note: Eastern Ukraine (Donetsk and Luhansk); fighting since 2014, much of it occupied by Russia.

pins.name: Kherson
pins.note: Southern Ukraine on the Dnipro; part-occupied since 2022.

pins.name: Zaporizhzhia
pins.note: South-east Ukraine; Europe's largest nuclear plant, occupied by Russia since 2022.

pins.name: Crimea
pins.note: Black Sea peninsula of Ukraine annexed by Russia in 2014.

pins.name: Nagorno-Karabakh
pins.note: Armenian-majority enclave inside Azerbaijan; Azerbaijan took full control in 2023.

pins.name: Chechnya
pins.note: Russian republic in the North Caucasus; wars of 1994–96 and 1999–2009.

pins.name: Catalonia
pins.note: North-east Spain, capital Barcelona; held an independence referendum in 2017.

pins.name: Anatolia
pins.note: The Asian peninsula of Turkey, between the Black and Mediterranean Seas.

pins.name: Aleppo
pins.note: Northern Syria; a major battleground of the civil war.

pins.name: Mosul
pins.note: Northern Iraq on the Tigris; held by ISIS 2014–17.

pins.name: Kirkuk
pins.note: Northern Iraq; oil city disputed between Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region.

pins.name: Mazar-i-Sharif
pins.note: Northern Afghanistan, near the Uzbek border.

pins.name: Levant
pins.note: The eastern Mediterranean coast: Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Palestine and Jordan.

pins.name: Darfur
pins.note: Western Sudan; conflict since 2003, renewed in the war that began in 2023.

pins.name: Tigray
pins.note: Northern Ethiopia; war between the federal government and the TPLF, 2020–22.

pins.name: Amhara
pins.note: Ethiopia's second-largest region; Lake Tana, source of the Blue Nile.

pins.name: Oromia
pins.note: Ethiopia's largest and most populous region, around Addis Ababa.

pins.name: Cabo Delgado
pins.note: Northern Mozambique; insurgency since 2017 near large gas projects.

pins.name: North Kivu
pins.note: Eastern DR Congo, on the Rwanda border; armed groups including M23.

pins.name: Ituri
pins.note: North-east DR Congo; ethnic and armed-group violence.

pins.name: Kachin
pins.note: Myanmar's northernmost state, bordering China and India; conflict between the army and the Kachin Independence Army.

pins.name: Mindanao
pins.note: Southern Philippines; the Bangsamoro autonomous region was set up in 2019.

pins.name: Senkaku Islands
pins.note: Uninhabited East China Sea islands run by Japan and claimed by China as the Diaoyu.

pins.name: Chabahar
pins.note: Iran's port on the Gulf of Oman; India runs the Shahid Beheshti terminal, a route to Afghanistan and Central Asia.

pins.name: Mallorca
pins.note: Spain's largest Balearic island (not Italy).

pins.name: Normandy
pins.note: North-west France (not Spain); D-Day landings of 1944.

pins.name: Sardinia
pins.note: Italian island in the Mediterranean (not France).

pins.name: Anadyr
pins.note: Russian Far East, west of the International Date Line: a day ahead of Nome.

pins.name: Nome
pins.note: Alaska, east of the Date Line: close to Anadyr in distance but a calendar day behind.

pins.name: Adriatic Sea
pins.note: Between Italy and the Balkans: Italy, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Albania border it.

pins.name: Black Sea
pins.note: Bordered by Ukraine, Russia, Georgia, Turkey, Bulgaria and Romania; reached through the Bosporus.

pins.name: Caspian Sea
pins.note: The world's largest lake: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan border it; the Volga drains into it.

pins.name: North Sea
pins.note: Between Britain and the continent: UK, Norway, Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium and France.

pins.name: Gulf of Aqaba
pins.note: Between Sinai and Arabia: Egypt, Israel, Jordan and Saudi Arabia border it.

pins.name: Dead Sea
pins.note: On the Jordan–Israel–West Bank border; the lowest land point on Earth.

pins.name: SUMED pipeline
pins.note: Egypt: carries crude from Ain Sukhna on the Gulf of Suez to Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean, alongside the Suez Canal.

pins.name: East China Sea
pins.note: Between China, Taiwan, Japan and South Korea.

pins.name: Aral Sea
pins.note: Kazakhstan–Uzbekistan; shrank after Soviet irrigation diverted the Amu Darya and Syr Darya.

pins.name: Lake Baikal
pins.note: Siberia; the world's deepest and oldest lake.

pins.name: Lake Victoria
pins.note: Africa's largest lake (Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania); source of the White Nile.

pins.name: Lake Tanganyika
pins.note: A Rift Valley lake, the second deepest in the world: Tanzania, DR Congo, Burundi and Zambia.

pins.name: Lake Turkana
pins.note: Northern Kenya, its tip in Ethiopia; the world's largest desert lake, fed by the Omo.

pins.name: Lake Faguibine
pins.note: Mali, near Timbuktu; fed by the Niger floods, now mostly dry.

pins.name: Tonle Sap
pins.note: Cambodia; its river reverses flow when the Mekong floods.

pins.name: Lagoa dos Patos
pins.note: Southern Brazil; the largest coastal lagoon in South America.

pins.name: Thames
pins.note: Flows east through London into the North Sea.

pins.name: Volga delta
pins.note: Europe's longest river ends in the Caspian Sea.

pins.name: Zambezi mouth
pins.note: Reaches the Indian Ocean in Mozambique; Victoria Falls and the Kariba dam are upstream.

pins.name: Okavango Delta
pins.note: Botswana; an inland delta that never reaches the sea.

pins.name: Congo Basin
pins.note: Central Africa; holds the world's largest tropical peatland (Cuvette Centrale).

pins.name: Kikori Basin
pins.note: Papua New Guinea; a forested river basin (the Prelims 2024 distractor for the largest tropical peatland).

pins.name: Guiana Highlands
pins.note: Venezuela, Guyana and Brazil; ancient tablelands; Angel Falls.

pins.name: Abyssinian Highlands
pins.note: Ethiopia; the Blue Nile rises at Lake Tana.

pins.name: Patagonia
pins.note: Southern Argentina and Chile; a cold desert in the rain shadow of the Andes.

pins.name: Vosges
pins.note: Mountains of north-east France, west of the Rhine rift valley.

pins.name: Tungurahua
pins.note: An active volcano in the Ecuadorian Andes.

meta.name: World places in the news
meta.seo: World map of places in the news for UPSC Prelims
meta.desc: Places in the news on the world map for UPSC Prelims and GS2: conflict regions, seas and the countries around them, lakes, rivers and highlands, each with the PYQ that asked it.
meta.lead: Prelims asks where conflict regions are, which countries border a sea, and which lake or river is where. Every pin here was named in a PYQ. Tap a pin to read why it matters, then test yourself.

layerModules.name: Physical India
layerModules.seo: Physical map of India for UPSC Mains
layerModules.desc: Physical India map for UPSC Mains: Himalayan and peninsular ranges, plateaus, plains, desert, coasts and deltas, mountain passes and peaks, with a locate quiz and PYQ sketch drills.
layerModules.lead: Every geography answer rests on this frame: the young Himalayas in the north, the old peninsular block in the south, the alluvial plains between them, and the coasts and islands around. Switch layers, tap a feature, then test yourself.

layers.name: Mountains & hills
layers.note: The Himalaya–Karakoram arc is young fold mountains; the Aravallis are among the oldest ranges on Earth; the Vindhyas and Satpuras divide north from south India; the Western Ghats are a steep escarpment, the Eastern Ghats a broken line of hills.

layers.name: Plateaus, plains & desert
layers.note: The Deccan and Chota Nagpur plateaus hold most of India's minerals; the Indo-Gangetic plain is the agricultural core; the Thar is India's hot desert.

layers.name: Coasts & deltas
layers.note: The west coast is narrow and cut by estuaries; the east coast is broad, with the big deltas of the Ganga–Brahmaputra, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri.

layers.name: Passes
layers.note: Himalayan passes carry trade, pilgrimage and military routes; the Palghat Gap is the main break in the Western Ghats.

items.name: Karakoram Pass
items.note: Ladakh–Xinjiang; historic Silk Road branch.

items.name: Khardung La
items.note: Ladakh; road to the Nubra valley and Siachen.

items.name: Zoji La
items.note: Links the Kashmir valley with Ladakh; a tunnel is being built beneath it.

items.name: Banihal
items.note: Pir Panjal crossing between Jammu and the Kashmir valley.

items.name: Rohtang
items.note: Himachal Pradesh, Kullu to Lahaul; bypassed by the Atal Tunnel.

items.name: Shipki La
items.note: Himachal Pradesh–Tibet trade pass, along the Sutlej.

items.name: Lipulekh
items.note: Uttarakhand–Tibet; Kailash Mansarovar route; Nepal disputes the area.

items.name: Nathu La
items.note: Sikkim–Tibet; trade route and Kailash yatra route.

items.name: Bomdi La
items.note: Arunachal Pradesh, on the road to Tawang.

items.name: Palghat Gap
items.note: Break in the Western Ghats linking Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

items.name: Bhor Ghat
items.note: Western Ghats pass on the Mumbai–Pune route.

layers.name: Peaks
layers.note: Highest points of each block: K2 in the Karakoram, Kangchenjunga in the Himalaya, Anamudi in the south.

items.name: K2 (Godwin-Austen)
items.note: Highest peak in India's territory (Karakoram, in Gilgit-Baltistan).

items.name: Kangchenjunga
items.note: Highest peak of the Indian Himalaya, on the Sikkim–Nepal border.

items.name: Nanda Devi
items.note: Uttarakhand; core of a biosphere reserve.

items.name: Anamudi
items.note: Highest peak in peninsular India, Kerala.

items.name: Doddabetta
items.note: Highest point of the Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu.

items.name: Guru Shikhar
items.note: Highest point of the Aravallis, Mount Abu, Rajasthan.

layers.name: Islands
layers.note: Andaman & Nicobar are the peaks of a submerged range; Lakshadweep is coral atolls.

layers.name: Hills & ranges in PYQs
layers.note: Hill ranges and peaks Prelims has asked about, often as 'match the hills to the region'. Learn which block each belongs to: Himalaya, Purvanchal, Central Highlands or Peninsula.

items.name: Cardamom Hills
items.note: Kerala–Tamil Nadu; southern Western Ghats; not on the Coromandel coast.

items.name: Kaimur Range
items.note: Bihar–Uttar Pradesh–Madhya Pradesh; eastern end of the Vindhyas; not on the Konkan coast.

items.name: Mahadeo Hills
items.note: Madhya Pradesh; part of the Satpuras; Pachmarhi and Dhupgarh, the highest point of the Satpuras.

items.name: Mikir (Karbi Anglong) Hills
items.note: Assam; a detached part of the Meghalaya plateau.

items.name: Garo Hills
items.note: Meghalaya; Nokrek peak and biosphere reserve.

items.name: Barail Range
items.note: Assam (Dima Hasao), Nagaland and Manipur; Loktak Lake is not in it.

items.name: Dafla Hills
items.note: Arunachal Pradesh; Namdapha is not in them (it is on the Patkai).

items.name: Saramati
items.note: Nagaland's highest peak, on the Myanmar border.

items.name: Satmala Hills
items.note: Maharashtra; low hills south of the Tapi, running east from Ajanta.

items.name: Biligirirangan Hills
items.note: Karnataka; a tiger reserve linking the Western and Eastern Ghats.

items.name: Veliconda Range
items.note: Andhra Pradesh; residual hills of the Eastern Ghats on the Peninsular block.

items.name: Mahendragiri (Odisha)
items.note: Odisha; a residual Eastern Ghats peak on the Peninsular block.

items.name: Anaimalai Hills
items.note: Tamil Nadu–Kerala, south of the Palghat Gap; Anamudi, the highest peak in South India, is at their edge.

items.name: Maikal Range
items.note: Chhattisgarh–Madhya Pradesh; Amarkantak, source of the Narmada and Son.

items.name: Namcha Barwa (Tibet)
items.note: In Tibet, China, where the Yarlung Tsangpo (Brahmaputra) bends south into India; eastern anchor of the Himalaya. Not in the Garhwal Himalaya.

layers.name: Glaciers, valleys & islands in PYQs
layers.note: Himalayan glaciers and high valleys, and the island features Prelims asks about.

items.name: Bandarpunch glacier
items.note: Uttarakhand; feeds the Yamuna side of Garhwal.

items.name: Bara Shigri glacier
items.note: Himachal Pradesh, Lahaul-Spiti; one of the largest glaciers in the state; feeds the Chenab.

items.name: Milam glacier
items.note: Uttarakhand, Kumaon; source of the Gori Ganga.

items.name: Zemu glacier
items.note: Sikkim; the largest glacier in the Eastern Himalaya, at the foot of Kangchenjunga.

items.name: Gangotri glacier
items.note: Uttarakhand; the Bhagirathi rises at Gaumukh, its snout.

items.name: Aksai Chin
items.note: Part of Ladakh, held by China since the 1950s; India's boundary includes it.

items.name: Nubra valley
items.note: Ladakh; valley of the Shyok and Nubra rivers, north of Khardung La.

items.name: Barren Island
items.note: Andaman Sea; India's only active volcano.

items.name: Ten Degree Channel
items.note: Separates Little Andaman from Car Nicobar.

layerModules.name: Climate, monsoon & soils
layerModules.seo: Monsoon, climate & soil map of India for UPSC
layerModules.desc: Monsoon, climate and soil map of India for UPSC Mains: the two monsoon branches, rainfall extremes, the north-east monsoon, and the main soil regions, with PYQ sketch drills.
layerModules.lead: The monsoon arrives in two branches, gets blocked or squeezed by relief, and leaves a map of wet and dry places that decides soils, crops and hazards. These maps are schematic, as you would draw them in an answer.

layers.name: Monsoon branches
layers.note: Schematic. The Arabian Sea branch hits the Western Ghats and moves inland; the Bay of Bengal branch is funnelled into the North-East and turned west along the Himalaya, which is why Bihar's monsoon blows from the east (Purvaiya).

items.name: Arabian Sea branch
items.note: Brings heavy rain to the windward Western Ghats; the Deccan interior lies in rain shadow.

items.name: Bay of Bengal branch
items.note: Turns west along the Himalaya; rain decreases from east to west across the Ganga plain.

layers.name: Rainfall extremes
layers.note: Relief explains the extremes: the funnel-shaped Khasi hills catch the Bay branch, while Ladakh and western Rajasthan lie beyond the reach of moist winds.

items.name: Mawsynram
items.note: Among the wettest places on Earth, on the southern Khasi hills.

items.name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
items.note: Next to Mawsynram; record rainfall from orographic lifting.

items.name: Agumbe
items.note: Very wet windward slope of the Western Ghats, Karnataka.

items.name: Jaisalmer
items.note: Hot desert: the Arabian Sea branch runs parallel to the Aravallis and drops little rain.

items.name: Leh
items.note: Cold desert in the rain shadow of the Himalaya.

layers.name: North-east (winter) monsoon
layers.note: Tamil Nadu gets most of its rain from October to December, when retreating north-east winds pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal.

layers.name: Alluvial soils
layers.note: Approximate, by state. Deposited by Himalayan rivers; India's most widespread and fertile soil.

layers.name: Black (regur) soils
layers.note: Approximate, by state. Weathered Deccan basalt; holds moisture and suits cotton.

layers.name: Red & yellow soils
layers.note: Approximate, by state. On old crystalline rocks of the eastern and southern peninsula; low in nitrogen.

layers.name: Laterite soils
layers.note: Approximate, by state. Leached in hot, very wet areas; used for cashew, tea and coffee.

layers.name: Desert soils
layers.note: Sandy, saline and low in organic matter.

layerModules.name: Hazard zones
layerModules.seo: Disaster hazard zone map of India for UPSC
layerModules.desc: Hazard map of India for UPSC Mains: seismic zone V, cyclone-prone coasts, flood-, drought- and landslide-prone states, and major disasters since 1984, with PYQ sketch drills.
layerModules.lead: Disaster management answers score with a quick vulnerability sketch. These layers show where each hazard concentrates, at state level, and where the major disasters of recent decades struck.

layers.name: Seismic zone V
layers.note: Highest-risk zone in the long-standing BIS zoning (IS 1893). Shown by state: dark = whole state, light = parts. BIS has been revising the zoning, so check the current map before quoting it.

layers.name: Cyclone-prone coasts
layers.note: The east coast faces more and stronger cyclones; Arabian Sea cyclones are fewer but growing stronger as the sea warms.

layers.name: Flood-prone
layers.note: The Brahmaputra and Ganga plains flood almost every year; urban floods now add to this map.

layers.name: Drought-prone

layers.note: Two belts: the young, seismic Himalaya and the steep, rain-soaked Western Ghats.

layers.name: Major disasters
layers.note: Case studies UPSC answers often cite.

items.name: Bhopal gas leak (1984)
items.note: Industrial disaster; led to new environmental and liability laws.

items.name: Latur earthquake (1993)
items.note: Struck the 'stable' Deccan plateau, in what was then rated a low-risk zone.

items.name: Odisha super cyclone (1999)
items.note: About 10,000 deaths; Odisha's later preparedness became a model.

items.name: Bhuj earthquake (2001)
items.note: Together with the 2004 tsunami, pushed India towards the Disaster Management Act, 2005.

items.name: Indian Ocean tsunami (2004)
items.note: Hit the Tamil Nadu coast (Nagapattinam) and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

items.name: Mumbai floods (2005)
items.note: Extreme rain on a city that had built over drains and the Mithi river.

items.name: Kedarnath (2013)
items.note: Cloudburst and glacial lake burst in Uttarakhand.

items.name: Chennai floods (2015)
items.note: Encroached lakes and wetlands turned heavy rain into a flood.

items.name: Kerala floods (2018)
items.note: Heaviest floods in Kerala in about a century; landslides across the Ghats.

items.name: Joshimath subsidence (2023)
items.note: Town sinking on old landslide debris; questions over Himalayan construction.

items.name: Wayanad landslides (2024)
items.note: Deadly landslides after extreme rain in the Western Ghats.

layerModules.name: Resources & agriculture

items.name: Korba

items.note: Odisha (Mahanadi valley).

items.name: Singrauli
items.note: Madhya Pradesh–Uttar Pradesh; India's 'energy capital'.

items.name: Singareni

items.name: Neyveli

items.name: Noamundi

layerModules.name: Society & polity on the map
layerModules.seo: Fifth & Sixth Schedule, Article 371 and new states map
layerModules.desc: Polity and society map of India for UPSC Mains: Fifth and Sixth Schedule states, Article 371 special provisions, states formed after 1956, Union Territories and sex-ratio extremes.
layerModules.lead: Federalism, tribal and social justice questions often turn on where a provision applies. These layers map the Schedules, the Article 371 states, India's newer states and its Union Territories.

layers.name: Sixth Schedule
layers.note: Autonomous district councils in tribal areas of four North-Eastern states (Article 244(2)). Ladakh's demand for it is a live issue.

layers.name: Fifth Schedule
layers.note: Scheduled Areas in ten states (Article 244(1)), with Tribes Advisory Councils and the PESA Act, 1996.

layers.name: Article 371 states
layers.note: Special provisions for particular states, from development boards (371) to protection of customary law (371A Nagaland, 371G Mizoram). Tap a state for its clause.

stateNotes.Maharashtra: Article 371(2): development boards for Vidarbha, Marathwada and the rest of the state.
stateNotes.Gujarat: Article 371(2): development boards for Saurashtra and Kutch.
stateNotes.Nagaland: Article 371A: Parliament's laws on Naga religion, customary law, and land and resources apply only if the Assembly agrees.
stateNotes.Assam: Article 371B: a committee of the Assembly for the tribal areas.
stateNotes.Manipur: Article 371C: a committee of the Assembly for the hill areas.
stateNotes.Andhra Pradesh: Article 371D: equitable opportunities in jobs and education; 371E: a central university.
stateNotes.Sikkim: Article 371F: terms of Sikkim's merger in 1975, protecting existing laws.
stateNotes.Mizoram: Article 371G: protection of Mizo religion, customary law, and land, as in Nagaland.
stateNotes.Arunachal Pradesh: Article 371H: the Governor's special responsibility for law and order.
stateNotes.Goa: Article 371I: an Assembly of at least 30 members.
stateNotes.Karnataka: Article 371J: special provisions for the Hyderabad–Karnataka (Kalyana Karnataka) region.

layers.note: India's longest land border, guarded by the BSF; riverine stretches are hard to fence.

layers.name: Myanmar border (Assam Rifles)
layers.note: Guarded by the Assam Rifles; the Free Movement Regime and drug trafficking are key issues.

layers.name: Left Wing Extremism
layers.note: The core belt has shrunk sharply; check the latest MHA list of affected districts before quoting numbers.

groups.label: Affected earlier or at lower intensity

layers.name: Coastal states & UTs
layers.note: Nine coastal states and four coastal UTs; coastal security was rebuilt after 26/11.

groups.label: Coastal states & UTs
items: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

layers.name: Security hotspots
layers.note: Places that recur in security answers.

items.name: Siachen
items.note: Highest battlefield; held by India since 1984 (Actual Ground Position Line).

items.name: Galwan valley
items.note: Ladakh; India–China clash, June 2020.

items.name: Pangong Tso
items.note: Ladakh; lake on the LAC, site of the 2020 stand-off.

items.name: Kargil
items.note: 1999 war against Pakistani intrusion.

items.name: Uri
items.note: 2016 attack, followed by surgical strikes.

items.name: Pulwama
items.note: 2019 attack, followed by the Balakot strike.

items.name: Pathankot
items.note: 2016 air base attack.

items.name: Mumbai (26/11)
items.note: 2008 sea-borne attack that reshaped coastal security.

items.name: Siliguri Corridor
items.note: The narrow 'Chicken's Neck' linking the North-East to the rest of India.

items.name: Doklam
items.note: India–China stand-off on Bhutanese territory, 2017.

items.name: Tawang
items.note: Arunachal Pradesh; China claims it.

items.name: Sir Creek
items.note: Disputed estuary on the Gujarat–Sindh boundary.

layers.name: Cross-border links
layers.note: Bridges, rail lines and corridors to neighbours that Prelims asked about in 2026. Kaladan and the IMT Trilateral Highway are India–ASEAN projects; the Agartala–Akhaura line links India and Bangladesh.

items.name: Maitri Setu (Feni river)
items.note: Tripura; bridge over the Feni linking Sabroom (India) with Ramgarh (Bangladesh).

items.name: Jhulaghat bridge
items.note: Uttarakhand, Pithoragarh; suspension bridge over the Mahakali to Nepal, not Myanmar.

items.name: Mechi bridge
items.note: West Bengal; links the Panitanki bypass with Kakarvitta in Nepal.

items.name: Agartala–Akhaura rail
items.note: Tripura; rail link to Akhaura in Bangladesh, an India–Bangladesh project.

items.name: Zorinpui (Kaladan road end)
items.note: Mizoram; where the Kaladan road from Paletwa enters India.

items.name: Sittwe port (Myanmar)
items.note: Myanmar; Kaladan Multi-Modal project port, linked by river and road to Mizoram.

items.name: Moreh (IMT highway)
items.note: Manipur; start of the India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway to Mae Sot.

layerModules.name: Environment overlays
layerModules.seo: Ramsar sites, tiger reserves & biosphere reserves map
layerModules.desc: Environment map of India for UPSC Mains: selected Ramsar sites, tiger reserves, UNESCO biosphere reserves, mangroves and coral reefs, with PYQ sketch drills. Selected sites, approximate locations.
layerModules.lead: Conservation answers are stronger with two or three correctly placed examples. These layers show selected, well-known sites, not complete lists, which change every year; pins are approximate.

layers.name: Ramsar sites (selected)
layers.note: Wetlands of international importance. Chilika and Keoladeo were India's first, in 1981; the list grows every year.

items.name: Chilika Lake
items.note: Odisha; brackish lagoon; one of India's first two Ramsar sites (1981).

items.name: Keoladeo
items.note: Rajasthan; bird sanctuary; first Ramsar sites with Chilika (1981).

items.name: Wular Lake
items.note: Jammu & Kashmir; large freshwater lake on the Jhelum.

items.name: Loktak Lake
items.note: Manipur; floating phumdis and Keibul Lamjao park.

items.name: Sambhar Lake
items.note: Rajasthan; India's largest inland salt lake.

items.name: Vembanad-Kol
items.note: Kerala; backwaters and below-sea-level farming.

items.name: East Kolkata Wetlands
items.note: West Bengal; treats the city's sewage through fisheries.

items.name: Sundarban Wetland
items.note: West Bengal; largest Ramsar site in India.

items.name: Bhitarkanika
items.note: Odisha; mangroves and saltwater crocodiles.

items.name: Point Calimere
items.note: Tamil Nadu; coastal wetland for migratory birds.

items.name: Harike
items.note: Punjab; at the Beas–Sutlej confluence.

items.name: Deepor Beel
items.note: Assam; Brahmaputra floodplain lake near Guwahati.

layers.name: Tiger reserves (selected)
layers.note: Project Tiger began in 1973 with Jim Corbett among the first reserves.

items.name: Jim Corbett
items.note: Uttarakhand; India's first national park (1936).

items.name: Kanha
items.note: Madhya Pradesh; saved the hard-ground barasingha.

items.name: Ranthambore
items.note: Rajasthan; dry deciduous forest.

items.name: Sundarbans Tiger Reserve
items.note: West Bengal; the only mangrove tiger habitat.

items.name: Periyar
items.note: Kerala; Western Ghats.

items.name: Bandipur
items.note: Karnataka; part of the Nilgiri landscape.

items.name: Kaziranga
items.note: Assam; also home to most of the world's one-horned rhinos.

items.name: Tadoba-Andhari
items.note: Maharashtra.

items.name: Panna
items.note: Madhya Pradesh; tigers reintroduced after local extinction; affected by the Ken–Betwa link.

items.name: Simlipal
items.note: Odisha; also a biosphere reserve.

items.name: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam
items.note: Andhra Pradesh–Telangana; India's largest tiger reserve.

items.name: Manas
items.note: Assam; World Heritage Site on the Bhutan border.

layers.name: Biosphere reserves (all 18)
layers.note: India's 18 biosphere reserves, set up under UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere idea. Most are also on UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves; check the current count before you write it.

items.name: Nilgiri
items.note: India's first biosphere reserve (1986); first in the UNESCO network (2000).

items.name: Gulf of Mannar
items.note: Tamil Nadu; coral reefs, sea grass and dugongs.

items.name: Sunderban
items.note: West Bengal; mangroves.

items.name: Nanda Devi
items.note: Uttarakhand; high Himalaya.

items.name: Nokrek
items.note: Meghalaya; wild citrus gene pool.

items.name: Pachmarhi
items.note: Madhya Pradesh; Satpura range.

items.name: Similipal
items.note: Odisha.

items.name: Achanakmar-Amarkantak
items.note: Madhya Pradesh–Chhattisgarh; source of the Narmada and Son.

items.name: Great Nicobar
items.note: Tropical island forests; the Great Nicobar project is debated.

items.name: Agasthyamala
items.note: Kerala–Tamil Nadu; Western Ghats.

items.name: Khangchendzonga
items.note: Sikkim; also a mixed World Heritage Site.

items.name: Panna
items.note: Madhya Pradesh; added in 2020.

items.name: Manas
items.note: Assam, on the Bhutan border; also a tiger reserve and World Heritage Site.

items.name: Dibru-Saikhowa
items.note: Assam, south of the Brahmaputra; feral horses, white-winged wood duck.

items.name: Dehang-Dibang
items.note: Arunachal Pradesh, Siang and Dibang valleys.

items.name: Kachchh
items.note: Gujarat; the largest biosphere reserve; Rann of Kutch, wild ass.

items.name: Cold Desert
items.note: Himachal Pradesh, Pin valley and Spiti; snow leopard.

items.name: Seshachalam
items.note: Andhra Pradesh, Eastern Ghats; red sanders.

layers.name: Mangroves
layers.note: Mangroves buffer coasts against cyclones and storm surges.

items.name: Sundarbans mangroves
items.note: West Bengal; largest mangrove forest in the world (shared with Bangladesh).

items.name: Bhitarkanika mangroves
items.note: Odisha; second-largest in India.

items.name: Coringa (Godavari delta)
items.note: Andhra Pradesh.

items.name: Pichavaram
items.note: Tamil Nadu; reduced 2004 tsunami damage behind it.

items.name: Gulf of Kutch mangroves
items.note: Gujarat; arid-zone mangroves.

layers.name: Coral reefs
layers.note: India's four main reef areas; warming seas cause bleaching.

items.name: Gulf of Mannar reefs
items.note: Fringing reefs around 21 islands, Tamil Nadu.

items.name: Gulf of Kutch reefs
items.note: Gujarat; India's first marine national park.

items.name: Lakshadweep atolls
items.note: Coral atolls.

items.name: Andaman & Nicobar reefs
items.note: India's richest reefs.

layers.name: Parks & sanctuaries in PYQs
layers.note: National parks, tiger reserves and sanctuaries that Prelims has named, from Kerala's Agasthyamala hills to Arunachal's Namdapha. Learn each with its state, its hill range and its flagship species.

items.name: Silent Valley NP
items.note: Kerala, in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve; tropical evergreen forest, lion-tailed macaque; saved from a dam on the Kunthipuzha in the 1980s.

items.name: Namdapha NP & TR
items.note: Arunachal Pradesh, on the Patkai hills near Myanmar; home to tiger, leopard, clouded leopard and snow leopard.

items.name: Dampa TR
items.note: Mizoram's largest protected area, on the Bangladesh border.

items.name: Gumti WLS
items.note: Tripura (not Sikkim, as one PYQ pair claimed); around the Gumti reservoir.

items.name: Keibul Lamjao NP
items.note: Manipur, on Loktak Lake; the world's only floating national park, on phumdis; home of the sangai deer.

items.name: Neora Valley NP
items.note: West Bengal (Kalimpong), next to Sikkim and Bhutan; red panda habitat.

items.name: Sultanpur NP
items.note: Haryana, near Gurugram; a bird sanctuary and Ramsar site.

items.name: Pakke (Pakhui) TR
items.note: Arunachal Pradesh, between the Kameng and Pakke rivers; known for hornbill conservation.

items.name: Valley of Flowers NP
items.note: Uttarakhand, Chamoli; alpine meadows; with Nanda Devi NP a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

items.name: Neyyar WLS
items.note: Kerala; part of the Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve.

items.name: Peppara WLS
items.note: Kerala; part of the Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve.

items.name: Shendurney WLS
items.note: Kerala; part of the Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve.

items.name: Kalakad-Mundanthurai TR
items.note: Tamil Nadu; the Tamil Nadu side of the Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve.

items.name: Nagarhole NP
items.note: Karnataka, Kodagu and Mysuru; part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

items.name: Papikonda NP
items.note: Andhra Pradesh, along the Godavari gorge in the Eastern Ghats.

items.name: Sathyamangalam TR
items.note: Tamil Nadu, Erode; the corridor where the Western and Eastern Ghats meet.

items.name: Mudumalai TR
items.note: Tamil Nadu, Nilgiris; joins Bandipur and Wayanad.

items.name: Mukurthi NP
items.note: Tamil Nadu, Nilgiris; shola grasslands; Nilgiri tahr.

items.name: Askot WLS
items.note: Uttarakhand, Pithoragarh, near Nepal; musk deer.

items.name: Gangotri NP
items.note: Uttarakhand, Uttarkashi; contains the Gangotri glacier; snow leopard.

items.name: Kishanpur WLS
items.note: Uttar Pradesh; part of the Dudhwa Tiger Reserve in the Terai.

items.name: Tal Chhapar WLS
items.note: Rajasthan, Churu; blackbuck and raptors.

items.name: Desert NP
items.note: Rajasthan, Jaisalmer and Barmer; Great Indian Bustard.

items.name: Kuno NP
items.note: Madhya Pradesh; cheetahs from Namibia and South Africa released here since 2022.

items.name: Madhav NP & TR
items.note: Madhya Pradesh, Shivpuri; declared a tiger reserve in 2025; Sakhya Sagar Ramsar site lies inside.

items.name: Sariska TR
items.note: Rajasthan, Aravallis; tigers were reintroduced after they disappeared around 2004.

items.name: Nallamala forest
items.note: Andhra Pradesh and Telangana; the Nallamala hills hold the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve.

items.name: Seshachalam hills
items.note: Andhra Pradesh, near Tirupati; biosphere reserve; red sanders.

layers.name: Lakes & wetlands in PYQs
layers.note: Lakes and wetlands from Prelims: freshwater, brackish and saline, natural and man-made. Note which are Ramsar sites.

items.name: Kolleru Lake
items.note: Andhra Pradesh, between the Godavari and Krishna deltas; freshwater; Ramsar site.

items.name: Pulicat Lake
items.note: Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu border; India's second-largest brackish lagoon; Sriharikota lies on its barrier island.

items.name: Kanwar (Kabartal)
items.note: Bihar, Begusarai; Bihar's first Ramsar site; an oxbow lake of the Gandak.

items.name: Hokera wetland
items.note: Jammu and Kashmir, near Srinagar; Ramsar site in the Jhelum basin.

items.name: Renuka Lake
items.note: Himachal Pradesh, Sirmaur; the state's largest natural lake; Ramsar site.

items.name: Rudrasagar Lake
items.note: Tripura; Ramsar site with the Neermahal lake palace.

items.name: Sasthamkotta Lake
items.note: Kerala, Kollam; the state's largest freshwater lake; Ramsar site.

items.name: Didwana Lake
items.note: Rajasthan, Nagaur; saline lake. Prelims 2021 grouped Didwana, Kuchaman, Sargol and Khatu as saline lakes.

items.name: Kuchaman Lake
items.note: Rajasthan; saline lake near Sambhar.

items.name: Kodaikanal Lake
items.note: Tamil Nadu, Palani hills; a man-made lake (1863).

items.name: Nainital Lake
items.note: Uttarakhand, Kumaon; a natural lake.

items.name: Sakhya Sagar
items.note: Madhya Pradesh, inside Madhav National Park; Ramsar site.

items.name: Doyang Lake
items.note: Nagaland, Wokha; reservoir where Amur falcons stop each autumn on their flight from Mongolia to Africa; protected by local communities.

layerModules.name: Rivers in detail
layerModules.h1: Rivers in detail: tributaries, dams and waterfalls
layerModules.seo: Rivers of India map for UPSC Prelims: tributaries, dams, waterfalls
layerModules.desc: India's river detail for UPSC Prelims and Mains: Godavari, Krishna and Brahmaputra tributaries, Eastern Ghats rivers, reservoirs and waterfalls, each linked to the PYQ that asked it.
layerModules.lead: Prelims keeps asking which tributary joins which river, which reservoir sits on which river, and which waterfall is where. Each pin here marks a confluence, a dam or a fall, with the PYQ that asked it. Pair this with the drainage module for the big river systems.

layers.name: Peninsular tributaries
layers.note: Pins mark where each tributary joins the main river.

items.name: Indravati joins Godavari
items.note: Indravati rises in Odisha's Kalahandi, flows through Chhattisgarh's Bastar and meets the Godavari on the Maharashtra–Telangana border.

items.name: Pranahita joins Godavari
items.note: Formed by the Wardha and Wainganga; joins the Godavari at Kaleshwaram.

items.name: Manjira joins Godavari
items.note: Rises in Maharashtra's Balaghat range; joins the Godavari near Kandakurthi.

items.name: Tungabhadra joins Krishna
items.note: Formed by the Tunga and Bhadra in Karnataka; Hampi lies on its bank.

items.name: Malaprabha joins Krishna
items.note: Joins the Krishna at Kudalasangama; Badami and Pattadakal lie in its basin.

items.name: Ghataprabha reservoir
items.note: Karnataka, Hidkal dam on the Ghataprabha, a Krishna tributary.

layers.name: East-flowing rivers
layers.note: Rivers that rise in the Eastern Ghats or Chota Nagpur and reach the Bay of Bengal on their own. Pins mark the river mouth unless noted.

items.name: Vamsadhara
items.note: Rises in Odisha's Eastern Ghats; reaches the sea at Kalingapatnam; Odisha–Andhra water dispute.

items.name: Nagavali
items.note: Rises in Odisha's Kalahandi; reaches the sea near Srikakulam.

items.name: Pennar mouth
items.note: Rises in Karnataka's Nandi hills; reaches the sea near Nellore.

items.name: Gandikota canyon (Pennar)
items.note: Andhra Pradesh, Kadapa; the Pennar cuts a gorge through the Erramala hills.

items.name: Subarnarekha mouth
items.note: Rises near Ranchi on the Chota Nagpur plateau; reaches the sea on the Odisha–West Bengal border.

layers.name: Brahmaputra & Barak
layers.note: The Siang, Dibang and Lohit meet near Sadiya to form the Brahmaputra; the Barak drains south Assam and Manipur.

items.name: Dibang
items.note: Arunachal Pradesh; joins the Siang near Sadiya; site of the Dibang multipurpose project.

items.name: Lohit
items.note: Arunachal Pradesh; enters from Tibet; the Dhola–Sadiya (Bhupen Hazarika) bridge crosses it.

items.name: Subansiri
items.note: Largest Brahmaputra tributary from the north; Subansiri Lower hydro project on the Assam–Arunachal border.

items.name: Kameng
items.note: Rises near Tawang; called the Jia Bharali in Assam.

items.name: Barak at Silchar
items.note: Rises in Manipur; flows through Silchar into Bangladesh as the Surma and Kushiyara.

items.name: Teesta–Rangeet confluence
items.note: The Rangeet joins the Teesta on the Sikkim–West Bengal border.

layers.name: Ganga & Indus details
layers.note: Tributary details from the northern rivers.

items.name: Chandra and Bhaga meet (Chenab)
items.note: At Tandi in Lahaul the Chandra and Bhaga form the Chandrabhaga, the Chenab.

items.name: Gomti at Lucknow
items.note: A plains-fed Ganga tributary rising near Pilibhit; joins the Ganga downstream of Varanasi. Not a Himalayan river.

items.name: Banas joins Chambal
items.note: Rajasthan; the Banas rises in the Aravallis and is wholly in Rajasthan.

items.name: Tapi mouth
items.note: West-flowing rift-valley river; rises in Betul, reaches the Arabian Sea near Surat.

layers.name: Dams & reservoirs
layers.note: Reservoirs from Prelims: know the river and the state.

items.name: Gandhi Sagar (Chambal)
items.note: Madhya Pradesh; first of the Chambal valley dams.

items.name: Indira Sagar (Narmada)
items.note: Madhya Pradesh, Khandwa; India's largest reservoir by storage.

items.name: Maithon (Barakar)
items.note: Jharkhand–West Bengal; a Damodar Valley Corporation dam on the Barakar.

items.name: Aliyar
items.note: Tamil Nadu, Anaimalai foothills; part of the Parambikulam–Aliyar project.

items.name: Isapur (Penganga)
items.note: Maharashtra; dam on the Penganga, a Wardha tributary.

items.name: Kangsabati (Mukutmanipur)
items.note: West Bengal, Bankura; dam on the Kangsabati.

layers.name: Waterfalls
layers.note: Waterfalls Prelims has paired with rivers.

items.name: Jog (Gersoppa) Falls
items.note: Karnataka; the Sharavati drops about 250 m; Gersoppa is another name for it.

items.name: Hundru Falls
items.note: Jharkhand, near Ranchi; on the Subarnarekha.

items.name: Dhuandhar Falls
items.note: Madhya Pradesh, Bhedaghat near Jabalpur; on the Narmada, below the marble rocks.
